## K21 · K21-free-cost — K21: the free list's per-frame cost against R10 at the gate; the list's shape

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

Evidence: Ruled by architect-8 (.wash/local/K21-free-cost-ruling.md): K21 replaces the intrusive free list with a two-level bitmap before merging - level 0 one bit per frame equal to the table's None with set_owner the one writer, higher levels one bit per non-zero word, depth a constant of PHYSMAP_SIZE, take = lowest free frame by trailing_zeros, kernel_frame the highest, a free or claim touching one word a level, memory taken at boot and kernel-held, the audit replacing check_free_list; no links in frames, so the stale-mapping hazard is removed and the held M2 line is dropped. R10 re-measured at seed 13 both widths; report if p99 &gt; main + 2 ms. Forwarded to K21's implementer.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `567024bd08019df30519523dab7fd0e6` · 2026-10-03T07:24:09Z

> K21's measurement (detail .worktrees/k21/.wash/local/K21-r10-free-cost.md): at the gate's seed 13 each destruction frees ~4,270 frames and push_free costs 6.6/7.6 ms of the slowest destruction (1.55/1.78 us a free at three kframe writes; each kframe write ~0.43 us, the cost following the writes not the page) - the free list is the ~8 ms excess over main. With the head's PREV made meaningless (two writes a push) R10 p99 is 28,286 rv64 / 28,583 rv32 against 30,000 - under the bound, but main's is ~22,370 (margin ~7.6 ms) and p50 rose ~6 ms (24.5 vs 18.7). The implementer stopped to ask rather than merge with 1.4-1.7 ms of margin, given K16 (512 PIDs, 255 threads: more frames per destruction) and SMP (the lock) are next on this path. Fallbacks in the file: (1) a kframe helper computing each frame's address once (small); (2) a destruction splices its freed frames once, one write a frame, PREV filled lazily; (3) a singly linked list, one write a free, but a claim by address needs a walk (R12); (4) a two-level bitmap: a free touches no frame, a take is a bounded search - and no links live in frames, which removes the integrity hazard your M2 line and SMP1's shootdown precondition guard against. Your ruling: merge (a) as is with the margin stated, or take (2) or (4) first; my lean is (4) if its take stays O(1)-bounded (a 2-level bitmap over 2^20 frames is a few words of scan), since it also deletes the stale-mapping hazard rather than fencing it, and (2) otherwise. K21 runs its focused cases on (a) meanwhile; its merge waits on you.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `f6b18862e3d1e10674cea70426659610` · 2026-10-03T07:25:37Z

> K21 takes (4) before it merges, as you leaned. Design, page lines and measurements are in .wash/local/K21-free-cost-ruling.md.
> 
> Why:
> - (a) leaves 1.4-1.7 ms of margin with K16 and SMP next on R10's path.
> - (2) still writes every freed frame (~1.8 ms a destruction) and keeps kernel links inside free frames.
> - (4) writes no frame, and removes the stale-mapping hazard instead of fencing it: a free frame then holds nothing of the kernel's, so a stale mapping on another hart reaches only the next owner's data. The shootdown stays, for that data.
> 
> Design:
> - Level 0 has one bit per frame, equal to the ownership table's None, with set_owner the one writer of both. Each higher level has one bit per non-zero word below.
> - The depth is a named constant fixed by PHYSMAP_SIZE, so it counts as a kernel constant under R12, not a term in RAM.
> - A take is the lowest free frame (trailing_zeros, one word a level); the trace build's kernel_frame takes the highest. A free or a claim by address touches at most one word a level.
> - The bitmap's memory is taken at boot like the DMA pool and counted as kernel-held. The checked audit replaces check_free_list, and alloc-first-fit stays the recorded negative.
> 
> Re-measure R10 p50 and p99 at seed 13 on both widths against main's; if p99 is still more than 2 ms above main's, report before merging.
> 
> Rebase on main: 082e00ccf rewrote m2-usable-shell.md step 4. Keep main's step 4 and drop K21's edit of it.
> 
> Pages:
> - memory.md's free-list paragraph and its residual are rewritten as in the file;
> - the held M2 line ("a free frame holds the free list's link") is dropped, so nothing lands at K21's merge;
> - I will update SMP1's brief to match.
> 
> Not an owner choice.
